evidence.description: FIND-1001's fix independently re-verified ACCURATE and COMPLETE. REQ-117's corrected step-9 text (behavioral-spec.md lines 2618-2633, 'Corrected (2026-07-08, Phase 1c iteration-1 review FIND-1001)') now states self/spawn's real CLI entrypoint sets `process.exitCode = 1` at TWO sites -- its top-level `.catch` AND its `.then()` success handler's own `if (result.status !== "active") process.exitCode = 1` -- and this was re-confirmed byte-for-byte against the real file's lines 183-194 (`.then(({decision, result}) => { console.log(...); if (result) { console.log(...); if (result.status !== "active") process.exitCode = 1; } }).catch((e) => { ...; process.exitCode = 1; })`). REQ-117's corrected text also now explicitly and correctly frames lending's own exit-0-for-refused behavior as a DELIBERATE DIVERGENCE from this real precedent, not a mirror of it, with a clear, defensible stated reason (a routine per-pair refusal should not look like a daemon failure to an exit-code-watching monitor) -- this closes FIND-1001 cleanly, with no remaining mischaracterization and no remaining risk of an implementer copying the wrong site's check verbatim (REQ-117's own text now explicitly warns against exactly that).

evidence.description: NEW critical finding (FIND-1003), found during the broader sweep this iteration's manifest requested. REQ-117's own step 6 literally shows `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt({lenderId, borrowerId, nowMs})` as a single-argument call. But the REAL `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt(..., deps = {})` requires `deps.getCitizen` with NO fallback default (`const getCitizen = deps.getCitizen;`, unlike `ledgerFile`/`lockStatePath`/`gojoLogRows`, all of which DO default). Empirically confirmed this review by fresh execution against the real, unmodified function: calling it exactly as REQ-117's own step-6 text shows (one argument, no deps) throws `TypeError: getCitizen is not a function` immediately -- before any eligibility/sizing/disbursement logic runs. REQ-117's own text never mentions `getCitizen` anywhere (confirmed by a full-text grep of both spec files -- zero matches). This means REQ-117, as currently specified, describes an entry point that would throw on EVERY real wake where step 5 actually finds a candidate pair -- the exact scenario this REQ exists to make possible -- directly contradicting its own EARS clause ('genuinely INVOKED').

convergenceSignals.note: Both of round-1's fixes (FIND-1001's exit-code correction, FIND-1002's test-injection-seam clause) were independently re-verified this iteration and found genuinely accurate and complete for what they each targeted -- neither needs further rework. The broader sweep this iteration's manifest requested (beyond re-checking only the 2 prior findings) surfaced ONE new, critical, previously-undetected defect: REQ-117's own step 6 shows a single-argument call to `executeLoanIssuanceAttempt`, but the REAL function (already converged, sprint-2) requires a second `deps` argument whose `getCitizen` key has NO fallback default -- confirmed by fresh execution against the real, unmodified source this review, which threw `TypeError: getCitizen is not a function` exactly as REQ-117's own literal step-6 text would invoke it. This is more severe than either round-1 finding: it means REQ-117, as currently specified, would crash on every real successful wake, not merely fail a test fixture. Finding count dropped 2 -> 1 (a genuine convergence signal, not a regression), but is not yet zero -- FAIL, next iteration required to add the missing `getCitizen`/`gojoLogRows` wiring specification to REQ-117 (and a matching update to PROP-117c's own fixture-3 verification text).
